intro.text: Welcome to the guided tour of the Content Manager!

steps.text: This is the navigation of the Content Manager. It gives access to all content-types created beforehand in the Content-type Builder.
The content-types are organised in 2 categories, *Collection types* and *Single types*, to make it easier to find them. But feel free to also use the search button! 🔍
Here we have an example of a **Single type**, which can only have one entry.
Therefore, with Single types, we directly land on their **edit view**.
Let's see an example of a **Collection type** to compare!
"Article" is a **Collection type**. It can manage several entries.
We first land on the **list view**, where we can choose which entry to edit.
Let's explore the list view! 🚀
These are the 🔍 **search** and **filter** buttons to help you find specific entries in the table.
This dropdown allows you to display in the table the entries based on the language, called "**locale**", they're available in.
This is the **settings** button, from which you can decide which fields to display or not in the table. It also gives access to the configuration of the list view.
Let's try using all these buttons together!
Click here to filter the entries listed in the table.
Let's filter based on the "category" field!
Let's filter entries which category is "nature".
Click on *Add filter* to apply the new filter on the table.

We now have only 2 entries left in our filtered table!

Talking about the table, let's configure it so that it fits our preferences!
Click on the settings button.
Click here to display the "author" field in the table of entries.
Authors are now displayed in the table!
💡 If you want to define the displayed fields more permanently, you can set your preferences via the *Configure the view* button.
Now that we've explored the list view, let's discover the edit view by **creating a new entry** for "Article"!
Let's explore the edit view!
Here is the name of your entry and its status, "Draft". Note that the concept of draft is only available if **Draft & Publish** is enabled.
You can also see the **Draft** and **Publish tabs** which respectively allow you to edit the entry and see in read-only mode what the published entry looks like.
This dropdown allows you to switch between the **locales** in which the entry is available.
This button allows you to automatically reuse the content of one locale for another.

This button gives access to several other options for the entry, such as:
• **Edit the model**, to be redirected to the Content-type Builder
• **Configure the view**, to set up differently how the edit view fields are displayed
• **Content History**, a feature to see the edition history of the entry
• **Delete entry**, to delete the entry in one specific locale or all of them
These are the fields of the entry, which were defined in the Content-type Builder, and can be filled in here.

This is the area where you can **save** and **publish content**.

You can also click on **...** to add your content to a **release** (if Releases is available) as well as **unpublish the entry**.
Let's try some of those options, starting with filling in some fields. Let's start with a title!
steps.value: How I wrote my first article with Strapi

steps.text: Now let's choose a category for our new article.
Don't forget to **save** your changes!
Now let's create a French version of our article!
Let's translate the title in French.
steps.value: Comment j'ai créé mon premier article avec Strapi

steps.text: And let's add a category for this version as well!
And let's not forget to save again!

This is the Content
Manager in a nutshell!

Feel free to visit
[https://docs.strapi.io/](https://docs.strapi.io/)
for more info on Strapi ❤️

outro.text: Thank you for following this guided tour!
